crime: The last time {WITCH_NAME} steadied the ladder while her mother hung out the washing, her mother said, "I can manage on my own now." Within the week, her mother was gone.

In the prison, one girl walked the top of the upper railing at dusk while the others bathed, a glass of water balanced on her head, the way she had once walked her family's wire. Every evening {WITCH_NAME} stood in the courtyard beneath her, ready to stop her with Magic a hair above the stones if she ever slipped.
At supper, the girl stood up in front of the whole table in the dining hall and thanked her. A month without slipping. "You needn't stand beneath me anymore."

That dusk, {WITCH_NAME} did not wait beneath. She came out through the hall behind the railing and pushed the girl off. She stopped the glass of water a finger above the stones and let the girl fall past it.
Back from the showers, the prisoners found her lying on the path. In the trial court they ruled that she had slipped walking alone, with no one beneath to hold her.

Then one prisoner turned the glass over in her hands. It had fallen as far as the girl had, and there was not a chip in it. Only {WITCH_NAME}'s Magic could have caught it, and the prisoners understood that she had been up at the railing when the girl fell.
fields.epitaph: A glass never tells you it can manage without you.
fields.epithet: A Net Waiting to Be Needed
execution: The execution stand strapped her face up beneath a high iron rail. Along the rail came an iron walker, a giant glass brimming with water balanced on its head. Directly above her, it let the glass slip. The glass came straight down and landed base first on her chest, water slopping over her face. She heaved under it until she stopped, and the water ran off the edge of the stand. The iron walker went on alone to the end of the rail, never looking down.

magic.name: Hair's Breadth
magic.text: She can stop anything about to fall, break, spill or bloom, a hair before it happens.
